2. **You approve that exact purchase**, for example “Pay ₹69.” Approval belongs to your account and that checkout; changed totals require fresh approval.

4. **Clanker finishes checkout** and posts the order confirmation in the original thread.

In a channel, the payment page would authenticate the intended payer. Card details stay with the payment provider; Clanker receives references and payment status.

Banks may still require OTP or 3DS authentication, and individual merchant checkouts need verification.

**The Slack experience is feasible now. Optional card retention is the specific provider capability still to validate.**

content.text: so I want to know about this native card provider

**Kernel’s native provider lets an agent pay with your existing card using network tokens.** Its API identifier is `provider: "kernel"`.

Here’s the flow:

1. **Enroll your card privately.** A Kernel-hosted page collects your card and email. A `wallet` item represents that enrolled card. Kernel’s documentation says the original card number never reaches Kernel; the underlying storage partner isn’t named. [Wallet specification](https://github.com/kernel/kernel-python-sdk/blob/main/src/kernel/types/vaults/kernel_wallet_vault_item_spec.py)

2. **Prepare a purchase.** Clanker creates a `card` item containing the amount, currency and merchant checkout URL. Kernel obtains a replacement card number, expiry and one-time three-digit code, stored encrypted for checkout. [Card specification](https://github.com/kernel/kernel-python-sdk/blob/main/src/kernel/types/vaults/kernel_card_vault_item_spec.py)

3. **Approve it.** Visa requires a hosted approval using a Visa passkey. Mastercard requires no additional hosted approval in this integration. Clanker would still require your approval through the **Pay ₹X** flow. [API specification](https://api.onkernel.com/spec.json)

4. **Complete checkout.** Kernel fills the payment fields only on the configured merchant origin. Clanker submits checkout and checks the merchant’s order confirmation. Kernel itself doesn’t establish whether the merchant charged the card. [Payment state](https://github.com/kernel/kernel-python-sdk/blob/main/src/kernel/types/vaults/kernel_card_state.py)

For **Remember this card**, we retain the wallet. For **Use once**, we could remove the wallet and enrolled card after resolving the payment outcome. That involves temporary enrollment; there’s no documented native retention checkbox. [Deletion behavior](https://www.kernel.sh/docs/api-reference/vaults/delete-a-vault-item-and-invalidate-its-secret-value)

Two significant limits:

- **Issuer eligibility:** your bank must support the required network token. Supporting INR doesn’t establish support for your particular Indian card.
- **Published amount cap:** 50,000 minor units, which means **₹500 per INR purchase**. [Live schema](https://api.onkernel.com/spec.json)

Also, the payment token enters the browser during filling and can be read through unrestricted browser access, so Clanker must protect those observations. [Fill documentation](https://www.kernel.sh/docs/vaults/fill)

**The API and official SDK confirm this integration exists. Your card’s eligibility and Zepto compatibility remain untested.**

Kernel obtains a replacement card number, expiry and one-time three-digit code, stored encrypted for checkout. [Card specification](https://github.com/kernel/kernel-python-sdk/blob/main/src/kernel/types/vaults/kernel_card_vault_item_spec.py)

3. **Approve it.** Visa requires a hosted approval using a Visa passkey. Mastercard requires no additional hosted approval in this integration. Clanker would still require your approval through the **Pay ₹X** flow. [API specification](https://api.onkernel.com/spec.json)

4. **Complete checkout.** Kernel fills the payment fields only on the configured merchant origin. Clanker submits checkout and checks the merchant’s order confirmation. Kernel itself doesn’t establish whether the merchant charged the card. [Payment state](https://github.com/kernel/kernel-python-sdk/blob/main/src/kernel/types/vaults/kernel_card_state.py)

For **Remember this card**, we retain the wallet. For **Use once**, we could remove the wallet and enrolled card after resolving the payment outcome. That involves temporary enrollment; there’s no documented native retention checkbox. [Deletion behavior](https://www.kernel.sh/docs/api-reference/vaults/delete-a-vault-item-and-invalidate-its-secret-value)

Two significant limits:

- **Issuer eligibility:** your bank must support the required network token. Supporting INR doesn’t establish support for your particular Indian card.
- **Published amount cap:** 50,000 minor units, which means **₹500 per INR purchase**. [Live schema](https://api.onkernel.com/spec.json)

Also, the payment token enters the browser during filling and can be read through unrestricted browser access, so Clanker must protect those observations. [Fill documentation](https://www.kernel.sh/docs/vaults/fill)

**The API and official SDK confirm this integration exists. Your card’s eligibility and Zepto compatibility remain untested.**

**Native Kernel cannot guarantee “submit card details, then everything happens automatically” for every card.**

- **Enrollment:** Kernel’s hosted page collects **card details and email**. The wallet connects when the card is stored; payment also requires issuer support for its network token. Public docs do **not** establish that enrollment never requests OTP, identity verification or a passkey. [Official wallet specification](https://github.com/kernel/kernel-python-sdk/blob/main/src/kernel/types/vaults/kernel_wallet_vault_item_spec.py)
- **Eligible Mastercard:** Kernel explicitly says **no hosted cardholder purchase approval** is required. That removes Kernel’s separate purchase approval step, subject to merchant/bank authentication and compatibility.
- **Visa:** Kernel explicitly requires a **hosted `spend_approval` completed with a Visa passkey before issuing the one-time code**. Backend automation cannot replace that required cardholder action. [Official card specification](https://github.com/kernel/kernel-python-sdk/blob/main/src/kernel/types/vaults/kernel_card_vault_item_spec.py)

Do not promise zero extra steps. The defensible product promise is: **“Enter your card; Clanker handles checkout. Complete bank or card-network verification only when required.”**
